newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close up but outlook still negative.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close up but outlook still negative.

text.p: FCOJ futures settled firmer but below session highs as the market remained too weak to sustain any substantial gains, market sources said.
Local selling pressured benchmark September to a contract low of 73.50 cents a lb on Wednesday, where the market found support amid shortcovering.
Prices climbed over unchanged in the afternoon, and speculative buying emerged and elected stops which fueled prices to the day's highs.
The market drifted off the highs in thin afternoon trade as buying interest evaporated, and the market settled slightly over unchanged.
"We tried to make a run for it but the market is too weak to sustain any rallies," an analyst said. "There is no good news out there and there won't be for some time."
September settled 0.40 cent firmer at 74.80 cents after trading from 76.00 to 73.50 cents. The rest finished down 0.40 to 1.00.
An estimated 1,600 lots changed hands compated to Wednesday's official tally of 2,144 lots.
Liquiditiy has declined from the record open interest posted two weeks ago. As of Wednesday, open interest stood at 31,271 lots, off 241 lots from the previous session.
